To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the web can be a useful and reliable source of information, (ii) it is possible to extract large amounts of facts automatically from the web, (iii) the web can serve as a large scale knowledge source, (iv) it is possible, and useful, to extract facts from the web with high confidence, (v) it is possible (and useful) to automatically fuse information from multiple web sources to improve accuracy.

(1) the use of a large set of domain specific patterns is critical for high quality results, (2) the use of multiple sources of evidence for the same pattern is essential, and (3) the use of statistical techniques is necessary to handle noisy data and multiple sources.

(1) it is possible to build a system that automatically extracts a very large number of facts in a scalable manner, (2) the system is able to extract facts that are not found in existing knowledge bases, (3) the system is robust to the presence of noise, (4) the system is not sensitive to the order in which the documents are presented, and (5) the system can trade off recall and precision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and evaluation of a system that can automatically extract facts from large collections of web pages in an autonomous, domain independent, scalable, and accurate manner.
the design of systems that can automatically extract large collections of factual information from the Web, and fuse them into a single, reliable knowledge base.
developing scalable, domain independent, and autonomous systems that extract large collections of facts in a reliable manner from unstructured, semi-structured, and structured sources.
